trust_decision.summary: The HTTP/2 header-size and stall policy is decided per connection in H2Connection (accumulated HEADERS/CONTINUATION state) and per stream in H2Stream.sendData, but the only bound that actually holds is the decoded header-list accounting inside the HPACK codec (Hpack.decodeHeaders) plus a per-header-block timeout created from ConnectionSettings.maxHeaderListSize; that setting defaults to None and the shipped fix folds None to Int.MaxValue, so every builder/wiring site must populate it or the protection silently never fires.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'unbounded continuation frame accumulation'; this is the only place an un-terminated HEADERS frame is stored as pending header state, and the CONTINUATION cases at :276 and :287 append to that same list with no size or time bound (State field declared at :555-556).

fix_sites.entry_point: Every HTTP/2 header/trailer/push-promise decode reached through EmberServerBuilder.withHttp2 and EmberClientBuilder.withHttp2
EmberServerBuilder.withHttp2 (ALPN h2, prior-knowledge h2c, h1->h2c upgrade) and EmberClientBuilder.withHttp2
Same connection state: the State case class (:547-557) and initState (:559-577) gain the timeout-carrying header progress and stallStart
Stream body send used by both builders (sendMessageBody/sendData)
Header/trailer receive for both directions (MessageTooLong -> GOAWAY EnhanceYourCalm)
EmberServerBuilder.build; the same settings derivation is also required in runConnection (:435-465) and at the h1->h2c upgrade call (:529-540)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: ConnectionSettings.default.maxHeaderListSize is None (H2Frame.scala:532) and the shipped fix turns None into Int.MaxValue (fix.diff:85-87), so a solver can reasonably treat the enforcement as 'configured elsewhere': absent SETTINGS means unlimited per RFC 9113 6.5.2, the frame loop already 'has' a per-frame maxFrameSize check at :307/:340, and wiring maxHeaderSize into ConnectionSettings at three server call sites plus the client builder looks like builder plumbing rather than part of the frame-accumulation bug.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A healthy connection must not accumulate stall time: stallStart has to be cleared whenever a chunk is fully written, while a peer that only drip-feeds window credit must keep the original start. A fix that sets the stall start on every write and never clears it (or clears it only on stream close) tears down long-lived keep-alive connections after idleTimeout; one that clears it on any WINDOW_UPDATE is bypassed by a 1-byte drip.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Client-side connection accepts CONTINUATION frames for a header block with no time or size bound; the shipped fix constructs the client connection with Duration.Inf for the header-receive timeout, so only the server direction gets the ContinuationProgress timeout.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The advisory is about an Ember server accepting frames, the client only talks to a peer the application chose, and the fix itself passes Duration.Inf here (fix.diff:95), so a reader concludes client-side accumulation is deliberate.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package, different module: ember-core h2 vs EmberClientBuilder in ember-client (1 file away from the landing point's package)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: H2Client.impl keeps settings = ConnectionSettings.default, whose maxHeaderListSize is None, so a caller that takes the default gets an HPACK decoder built with Int.MaxValue; the fix does not change this default. H2Server.fromSocket has the same shape but no default value.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: H2Client.impl is private[ember], EmberClientBuilder is its only in-repo caller and passes explicit settings, and 'defaults are protocol defaults' is a plausible-sounding reason to leave the default unbounded.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package (ember-core/h2), 1 file from the landing point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Cap the bytes buffered in readNextFrame while waiting for a complete RawFrame (the 24-bit length field allows up to ~16 MiB per frame).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same accumulate-peer-bytes-until-complete pattern in the same function family a maintainer hardens for this advisory; a peer that dribbles a declared-length frame pins memory per connection.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Bound the reassembled header block (headers.headerBlock ++ all continuation fragments) before handing it to the decoder.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: That fold is exactly where a reviewer expects the size check to live; the shipped fix instead put the accounting inside the decoder, so a sibling written by a different contributor would plausibly sit here with its own limit and error mapping.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A single helper that derives h2 ConnectionSettings (including maxHeaderListSize) from maxHeaderSize and is used by every transport.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The fix duplicates the same settings construction in two functions with a third call site at :529-540; extracting a helper is the natural cleanup, and a maintainer adding a new transport would route through it.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Cap the accumulated CONTINUATION fragments in H2Connection.processFrame (or lean on the existing per-frame maxFrameSize check at :307/:340) and stop: the decoded list stays unbounded because HPACK indexed references cost almost no wire bytes and the decoder silently truncates at its own 65536-byte cap instead of erroring.
